Autonomously selected original question: What is the exact worst-case correlation gap of nonnegative weighted coverage functions when pairwise independence is imposed only on the edges of a k-colorable graph, or a graph of maximum degree k-1? Can the extremal gap persist with only linearly many tested pairs and with one-sided multiplicative errors in their second moments?

For finite V, a simple graph G=(V,E), x in [0,1]^V, define D_G(x) to consist of laws of S⊆V with P(i∈S)=x_i and P(i,j∈S)=x_i x_j for each ij∈E. Nonedges carry no restrictions, and this is not a dependency-graph definition. Let f_G(x)=max_{D_G(x)} E f(S), and f^+(x)=max over laws with only the marginal constraints. A weighted coverage function is f(S)=Σ_H w_H 1{S∩H≠∅}, w_H≥0, with a finite feature family. Restrict ratios to f^+(x)>0. The original question asks for the supremum of f^+(x)/f_G(x) over all finite such objects and χ(G)≤k, for every integer k≥1, and separately Δ(G)≤k-1. Approximate constraints replace edge equalities by P(i,j∈S)≤(1+δ)x_i x_j with fixed δ≥0.

The scope is coverage functions. No claim is made to solve the analogous question for arbitrary monotone submodular functions or to prove that the resulting contribution meets a conference's acceptance threshold.

# Frozen original: Slater's complete binary1-skew-tolerant Gray-code nonexistence conjecture

Primary recent source: Gabriel Sac Himelfarb and Moshe Schwartz, Improved Constructions of Skew-Tolerant Gray Codes, arXiv:2411.08233v1,12November2024, p1Introduction and p3Definitions4--5/discussion. Retrieved current primary record1November2026; cached fullPDF SHA256f4faff61b1a23517a2a1d99ef232e36b11dc0473e89fcd56716aa85601a4d5ff in intake. Source sentence: “Slater [21] conjectured that no complete skew-tolerant (Pn-compatible) Gray code exists for n>=7.” Mathematical typography normalized only.

## Exact frozen mathematical claim
For EVERY integer n>=7 there is NO cyclic listing s_0,...,s_(2^n-1) of all distinct binary n-vectors such that, with indices modulo2^n, successive vectors differ in exactly one coordinate, and if d_i is that coordinate between s_i and s_(i+1), then |d_(i+1)-d_i|=1 for every i, where coordinates are numbered1,...,n in their fixed LINEAR order.

A single literal cyclic complete code at some n>=7 disproves this universal conjecture. A proof of it must cover all n>=7, not just solver exhaustion at n9. A construction for a family missing words, noncyclic path, circular adjacency between coordinate1 and n, larger alphabet, or2-skew tolerance does not resolve the target.

## Current status and nearest results
Torsten Mue tze, Combinatorial Gray codes--an updated survey, arXiv:2202.01280v4,30July2024, Section3.9p15, states that no P_n-code exists for n7 and reports Dimitrov/Gregor/Luzar computer exclusion of n8. It discusses transition graphs, which for a complete cyclic listing must be connected; P_n compatibility therefore yields exactly P_n. It also mentions smaller n<=6 with a convention not fully consistent with the cyclic/noncyclic distinction in2411.08233; preserve and resolve that distinction during triage, not by changing this frozen >=7 cyclic claim.

Antoine Amarilli's current author-maintained open-question list https://a3nm.net/work/research/questions/ explicitly defines this CYCLIC/path-adjacency question and asks existence for n>=9, with last-seen-open2026. Amarilli et al., Gray Codes with Constant Delay and Constant Auxiliary Space, arXiv:2602.11791/current ICALP2026 paper DOI10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2026.160, likewise identifies1-skew existence as open. Recent2411.08233 gives complete binary2-skew/3-skew codes and incomplete1-skew codes of nonvanishing density, plus complete nonbinary codes; these are different quantified statements.

Searches1November2026 for exact1-skew phrase/current follow-ups found the above primary sources and an old encoder patent US7019673 with n9 examples whose equivalence has NOT been inspected. The latter requires actual semantic checking before any novelty claim. Bounded literature screening establishes open-supported, not exhaustive priority. This target is semantically distinct from all historical registry topics and from Hamiltonian-path backbite/rectangular-grid flip connectivity: here a complete cyclic hypercube Hamilton cycle must obey coordinate adjacency at every turn.

# Immutable original question — frozen before experiments

Source: Xiaoyu He, Nitya Mani, Jiaxi Nie, Nathan Tung, Fan Wei,
*New Sidorenko-type inequalities in tournaments*, arXiv:2512.11222v1,
Problem 3.23, printed page 17, retrieved 2026-11-01.
Primary URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.11222v1
Downloaded PDF SHA256: 987454c9429a3f6aa28acfb45e8555a23d86d73ea783701f8376bcc7d3259c40.

Verbatim mathematical statement (math typesetting transcribed):

> Problem 3.23. Let ℓ ≥ 1, and let Ĉ₂ℓ be the oriented cycle of length 2ℓ with alternating direction. Is Ĉ₂ℓ⁽²⁾ LTS or not?

Relevant original definitions, not changes to the question:

* Immediately preceding Corollary 3.21, a k-subdivision replaces every directed edge by a directed path of k edges oriented all in the original direction.
* Definition 3.1, printed page 7: LTS means there is ε=ε(D)>0 such that every n-vertex weighted tournament A=J/2+B, with spectral radius of the real skew-symmetric B at most εn, has t_D(A)≥2^{-e(D)}.
* Thus the full target is EVERY integer ℓ≥1 and ALL n and all sufficiently small skew perturbations that are weighted tournaments. Its cyclic edge word is (++--) repeated ℓ times. The length-four case gives the intended interpretation of the length-two alternating base.

No one value of ℓ, bounded n, finite evidence, necessary condition, or theorem restricted to regular tournaments resolves this original family. A global weighted-tournament lower bound would resolve the entire question more strongly. Novelty and significance remain to be reviewed.

# Frozen target: linear compress-with-another words

Primary Marek Szykula, Synchronizing Automata: Open Problems, EPTCS451 (2026), pp33-47, DOI10.4204/EPTCS.451.3; arXiv2608.24245v1 (2026-08-25), Conjecture6 in Section2.3, printed p36. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24245v1 . The conjecture asks a linear compress-with-another threshold for every state in a strongly connected synchronizing automaton. The full15-page primary text is supplied.

Precise frozen original: is there an absolute finite C such that for every n>=2, every finite nonempty alphabet Sigma, every complete deterministic n-state semiautomaton (Q,Sigma,delta) that is strongly connected and synchronizing, and every distinguished q in Q, there are p!=q and a word w in Sigma* with |w|<=C n and delta(q,w)=delta(p,w)? Synchronizing means some word maps all Q to one state; strong connectivity is reachability of every state from every other. The alphabet is unrestricted, not silently binary. Minimum such length is mu_A(q).

A positive resolution requires a single uniform C for all those quantified inputs. A negative requires a rigorously verified family with mu_A(q)/n unbounded, while both synchronizability and strong connectivity are proved for every parameter. A single long finite word, finite no-counterexample range, or non-strongly-connected quadratic construction does not resolve this O(n) statement. The source Proposition7 already proves quadratic thresholds without strong connectivity. Source Conjecture8 for Figure3 is a different special case and has an October all-parameter treatment, arXiv2610.07044; do not rediscover or claim that special case resolves Conjecture6.

Test structured nearly-permutation binary/ternary families and a bounded seeded mutation search for increasing mu(q)/n; use any candidate to propose an all-parameter family or invariant, not an empirical asymptotic claim. Symmetrically seek a directed-distance or set-expansion proof. Recheck current primary followups before advancing.
